name: figma-embedded-raster-card
story: A designer built a guest-card bug with a portrait square and two text layers on a transparent frame, and exported it as SVG - so the portrait came out the way Figma always writes a placed image, as a pattern fill.
idioms: the placed picture is NOT a positioned <image>: it is <rect id="Guest photo" fill="url(#pattern0_44_612)"/>

<pattern id="pattern0_44_612" patternContentUnits="objectBoundingBox" width="1" height="1"> holding <use xlink:href="#image0_44_612" transform="scale(0.5)"> - the scale maps source pixels into bounding-box units
the actual <image> with the base64 data: URI is parked LAST inside <defs>, carrying only width/height and xlink:href, never x/y
xmlns:xlink declared on the root only because an image is present, after xmlns
the layer name stays on the visible rect, not on the <image> in defs
frame with no fill exports with no backplate rect - the bug is transparent over video
no <?xml?> prolog, zero indentation, fill="none" on the root, uppercase hex, fill-opacity for layer alpha, xml:space="preserve" plus style="white-space: pre" on text
whyThisMatters: Every raster a Figma user places arrives through this pattern/use/defs indirection, so an importer that looks for <image> elements on the artboard finds a picture sitting in <defs> that paints nowhere by itself - and either offers no picture field at all, or offers one bound to a node the operator's swap can never show; it also checks that a portrait drawn inside the growable panel is treated as a follower rather than as the panel.
